semantic_correction.stem: Why are comprehensive dilated eye examinations important for people at increased risk for glaucoma?

options.A: Glaucoma can have no early symptoms, and a comprehensive dilated eye examination can detect disease before more vision is lost.
options.B: Glaucoma usually causes severe eye pain before optic-nerve damage, so asymptomatic high-risk adults can delay examination.
options.C: A routine blood test detects glaucoma earlier than an eye examination and is preferred for high-risk adults.
options.D: Glaucoma becomes detectable after major central vision loss, so examination before visual symptoms has little value.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current National Eye Institute guidance states that glaucoma often has no early symptoms and may progress so slowly that a person does not notice vision changes. NEI states that the way to find out whether glaucoma is present is a comprehensive dilated eye examination, and its detection statement says that detection in higher-risk individuals is best done through a comprehensive dilated eye exam. Early diagnosis and treatment can help protect remaining vision. Therefore option A explains why screening examinations are important even when a high-risk person feels well and sees normally.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Explain that glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and that comprehensive dilated eye examination is important for detection in people at increased risk.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — vision screening
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests asymptomatic glaucoma detection in higher-risk people without a correct-answer length or absolute-word cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reflects NEI's statements about absent early symptoms and dilated-exam detection.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Common glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and does not reliably announce itself with severe pain before damage.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Glaucoma detection depends on eye examination, not a routine blood test.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. The value of examination is precisely to detect disease before major symptomatic vision loss.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone accurately states both the asymptomatic nature of early glaucoma and the role of comprehensive dilated examination.
cueing_check: All four options are explanations of screening value of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
